p5s0.title: Hotel Bond
p5s0.text: Hotel Bond is a historic hotel, built in two stages in 1913 and 1921, in downtown Hartford, Connecticut by hotelier Harry S. Bond.

p5s1.title: Hotel Bond
p5s1.text: It is located near Bushnell Park, and was considered the grandest hotel in Hartford during its heyday.

p5s2.title: Hotel Bond
p5s2.text: The second section is a 12 story building attached to the 6 story first section.

p5s3.title: Hotel Bond
p5s3.text: A Statler Hotel opened in the area in 1954, creating competition, and the Bond Hotel company declared bankruptcy shortly after that.

p5s4.title: Hotel Bond
p5s4.text: It was bought by the California-based Masaglia Hotel chain, which began an incremental renovation program.

p5s5.title: Hotel Bond
p5s5.text: In 1964 it was sold to a Cincinnati, Ohio investment group which announced extensive renovation plans.

p5s6.title: Hotel Bond
p5s6.text: However, the financing plans fell through and the hotel was again in bankruptcy.

p5s7.title: Hotel Bond
p5s7.text: The building was sold at auction to the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Hartford in 1965, and it became the home of the Saint Francis Hospital School of Nursing.

p5s8.title: Hotel Bond
p5s8.text: The Bond Ballroom reopened in 2001, with the rest of the building becoming a Homewood Suites by Hilton in 2006.

p0s0.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s0.text: The discography of Rosanne Cash, an American singer-songwriter, consists of thirteen studio albums, six compilation albums, one tribute album, and 39 singles.

p0s1.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s1.text: The daughter of Johnny Cash, Rosanne Cash recorded her self-titled debut album in 1978 under the German label Ariola.

p0s2.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s2.text: After signing with Columbia Records in 1979, Cash's second studio album "Right or Wrong" was released.

p0s3.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s3.text: Its lead single "No Memories Hangin' Around" (a duet with Bobby Bare) reached the Top 20 on the "Billboard" Hot Country Songs chart.

p0s4.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s4.text: Cash's third studio release, "Seven Year Ache" (1981) gained major success when the title track peaked at number one on the "Billboard" Country chart, followed by "My Baby Thinks He's a Train" and "Blue Moon with a Heartache," which also reached the top spot.

p0s5.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s5.text: The album's follow-up effort, "Somewhere in the Stars" (1982) produced two Top 10 hits on the "Billboard" chart.

p0s6.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s6.text: After a 3-year hiatus, Cash issued "Rhythm & Romance" in 1985, which reached #1 on the "Billboard" Top Country Albums list.

p0s8.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s8.text: This included the number one single, "I Don't Know Why You Don't Want Me," which won the Grammy Award for Best Female Country Vocal Performance in 1986.

p0s9.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s9.text: Her sixth album, "King's Record Shop" was released in 1987.

p0s10.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s10.text: The album peaked at number six on the country albums chart and certified gold in the United States.

p0s11.title: Rosanne Cash discography
p0s11.text: The four singles released from "King's Record Shop" all reached number one on the "Billboard" Country chart between 1987 and 1988, including a cover of Johnny Cash's "Tennessee Flat-Top Box."

p1s0.title: Train discography

p1s1.title: Train discography
p1s1.text: The band independently released their eponymous debut studio album in 1996, two years after their formation.

p1s3.title: Train discography

p1s4.title: Train discography
p1s4.text: The album peaked at number 76 on the US "Billboard" 200 and was certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).

p1s5.title: Train discography
p1s5.text: In the period following the release of "Train", producer Brendan O'Brien started working with the band in a partnership that would last for three albums.

p1s6.title: Train discography

p1s7.title: Train discography

p1s8.title: Train discography
p1s8.text: "Drops of Jupiter (Tell Me)" also won an award for Best Rock Song at the 44th Grammy Awards.

p1s9.title: Train discography
p1s9.text: The album peaked at number six on the "Billboard" 200, earning a double platinum certification from the RIAA. "

p1s10.title: Train discography
p1s10.text: She's on Fire", the third single from "Drops of Jupiter", achieved moderate success in Australia and the UK.

p1s11.title: Train discography
p1s11.text: Train's third studio album, "My Private Nation", was released in June 2003.

p1s12.title: Train discography
p1s12.text: It peaked at number six on the "Billboard" 200 and was certified platinum by the RIAA.

p1s13.title: Train discography
p1s13.text: The album's first two singles, "Calling All Angels" and "When I Look to the Sky", peaked at numbers 19 and 74 respectively on the "Billboard" Hot 100.

p1s14.title: Train discography
p1s14.text: The band released their fourth studio album "For Me, It's You" in January 2006.

p1s15.title: Train discography
p1s15.text: The album peaked at number 10 on the "Billboard" 200 and spawned three singles.

p2s0.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s0.text: "I Love You Always Forever" is a song by British singer Donna Lewis.

p2s1.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s1.text: It was released in the United States in May 1996 as the lead single from her debut album, "Now in a Minute".

p2s2.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s2.text: Inspired by the H. E. Bates novel "Love for Lydia", it peaked at number five on the UK Singles Chart.

p2s3.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s3.text: Outside the United Kingdom, it peaked within the top ten of the charts in Australia, Austria, Canada, France, Germany, New Zealand, Norway, Switzerland and the United States.

p2s4.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s4.text: In the latter country, the song peaked at number two on the "Billboard" Hot 100, where it remained for nine weeks during the summer of 1996, kept from number one by Los Del Rio's "Macarena".

p2s5.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s5.text: Despite this, the song was number one on the Hot 100 Airplay chart for thirteen weeks and the "Billboard" Top 40 Mainstream chart for eleven weeks, becoming one of the most played songs of the 1990s.

p2s6.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s6.text: The song therefore is drawn for third place among songs with the longest runs at number two on the "Billboard" Hot 100 and drawn at second for the most weeks at the "Billboard" Top 40 Mainstream chart.

p2s7.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s7.text: In Australia, the single also peaked at number two on the ARIA Singles Chart.

p2s8.title: I Love You Always Forever
p2s8.text: In 2016, the song was covered by Australian pop singer Betty Who, peaking at number six on the ARIA Singles Chart.

p3s0.title: The Definition Of...
p3s0.text: The Definition Of... is the fifth studio album by American recording artist Fantasia.

p3s1.title: The Definition Of...
p3s1.text: It was released by RCA Records and 19 Recordings on July 29, 2016 in the United States and for online streaming worldwide on Apple Music a day earlier.

p3s2.title: The Definition Of...
p3s2.text: Fantasia worked with producers Ron Fair, Brian Kennedy, Neff-U, Jerome "J-Roc" Harmon and GRADES on the album.

p3s3.title: The Definition Of...
p3s3.text: The album featured two top ten singles on the US "Billboard" Adult R&B Songs airplay chart: "No Time for It", which peaked at number six, and "Sleeping with the One I Love" which peaked at number nine.

p3s4.title: The Definition Of...
p3s4.text: In order to further promote the album, Fantasia embarked on a tour with Anthony Hamilton called .

p3s5.title: The Definition Of...
p3s5.text: "The Definition Of..." received mixed to positive reviews from music critics.

p3s6.title: The Definition Of...
p3s6.text: The album peaked at number six on the US "Billboard" 200.

p3s7.title: The Definition Of...
p3s7.text: The album also topped that week's "Billboard" Top R&B Albums chart, and peaked at number two on the US Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart.

p3s8.title: The Definition Of...
p3s8.text: The album was also promoted with an US twelve-show tour titled The Definition Of... Tour, which started on November 16, 2016 and ended on December 4, 2016.

p3s9.title: The Definition Of...
p3s9.text: The third single "When I Met You" was released on January 17, 2017.

p4s0.title: Thomas Rhett discography
p4s0.text: American singer and songwriter Thomas Rhett has released three studio albums, one extended play and thirteen singles, including one as a featured artist.

p4s1.title: Thomas Rhett discography
p4s1.text: His debut album, "It Goes Like This", debuted in the top 10 of the "Billboard" 200 in 2013 and produced three number one singles on the "Billboard" Country Airplay chart.

p4s2.title: Thomas Rhett discography
p4s2.text: Rhett released his second album, "Tangled Up", in 2015 which peaked at number six on the "Billboard" 200.

p4s3.title: Thomas Rhett discography
p4s3.text: Four of the album's five singles reached number one, while the second single, "Die a Happy Man" became his first crossover success and highest-charting single on the "Billboard" Hot 100.

p4s4.title: Thomas Rhett discography
p4s4.text: His third album, "Life Changes", is due in 2017.

p4s5.title: Thomas Rhett discography
p4s5.text: Nine of Rhett's singles have received at least a Gold certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), with six going Platinum.

p5s0.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s0.text: American country artist Trisha Yearwood has released twelve studio albums, seven compilation albums, one additional album, forty one music videos, fifty-eight singles and has appeared on twenty eight albums.

p5s1.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s1.text: Yearwood's self-titled debut album was released in 1991, peaking at number two on the "Billboard" Top Country Albums chart and number thirty one on the Billboard 200.

p5s2.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s2.text: It became the first debut female country album to sell one million copies, eventually certifying double platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. "

p5s3.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s3.text: She's in Love with the Boy" became the first female debut single since 1964 to top the "Billboard" Hot Country Singles chart.

p5s4.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s4.text: The album would spawn an additional three singles, including "The Woman Before Me".

p5s5.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s5.text: Her second studio album was the critically acclaimed "Hearts in Armor" (1992).

p5s6.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s6.text: It spawned the top five country hits "Wrong Side of Memphis" and "Walkaway Joe".

p5s7.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s7.text: Her third studio record "The Song Remembers When" (1993) enjoyed similar success while the lead single reached number two on the Billboard country chart.

p5s8.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s8.text: A holiday album appeared before her platinum-selling fourth studio album "Thinkin' About You" (1995).

p5s9.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s9.text: Reaching the third position of the country albums chart and the top thirty of the Billboard 200, its first two singles topped the Hot Country Singles chart.

p5s10.title: Trisha Yearwood discography
p5s10.text: Her sixth studio album "Everybody Knows" (1996) spawned Yearwood's fourth number one single, "Believe Me Baby (I Lied)".

p6s0.title: Number 1's (Destiny's Child album)
p6s0.text: Following its release, "#1's" received positive reviews from music critics who praised the included material as the highlights of the group's music career.

p6s1.title: Number 1's (Destiny's Child album)
p6s1.text: However, its title was dismissed as many of the songs included on the track listing hadn't reached the top position of a major record chart; it was later acknowledged by "Billboard" magazine that the title was only used as a marketing strategy.

p6s2.title: Number 1's (Destiny's Child album)
p6s2.text: The compilation debuted and peaked on top of the US "Billboard" 200 album chart becoming the group's second album to reach number one in that country.

p6s3.title: Number 1's (Destiny's Child album)
p6s3.text: It further peaked at number one in Japan and number six in the UK while also reaching the top forty in many European countries.

p6s4.title: Number 1's (Destiny's Child album)
p6s4.text: The compilation received seven certifications by music trade organizations in different countries across the world.

p6s5.title: Number 1's (Destiny's Child album)
p6s5.text: It further spawned two singles: "Stand up For Love", which failed to appear on a major music chart, and "Check on It", which reached number one on the US "Billboard" Hot 100 and the top ten on many European charts.

p7s0.title: Dirt (Alice in Chains album)
p7s0.text: Dirt is the second studio album by the American rock band Alice in Chains, released on September 29, 1992, through Columbia Records.

p7s1.title: Dirt (Alice in Chains album)
p7s1.text: Peaking at number six on the "Billboard" 200, the album was also well received by music critics.

p7s2.title: Dirt (Alice in Chains album)
p7s2.text: It has since been certified four-times platinum by the RIAA and gone on to sell five million copies worldwide, making "Dirt" the band's highest selling album to date.

p7s3.title: Dirt (Alice in Chains album)
p7s3.text: It is the band's last album recorded with all four original members, as bassist Mike Starr was terminated from the band in January 1993.

p8s0.title: Uncle Charlie
p8s0.text: Uncle Charlie is the fourth studio album by Charlie Wilson and was released on February 17, 2009.

p8s1.title: Uncle Charlie
p8s1.text: It features production from Gregg Pagani, The Underdogs, Bigg D, T-Pain and L.O.S. da Maestro.

p8s2.title: Uncle Charlie
p8s2.text: It features guest appearances from Snoop Dogg, Jamie Foxx and T-Pain.

p8s3.title: Uncle Charlie
p8s3.text: The first two singles from the album are "Supa Sexxy" and "There Goes My Baby", the latter receiving major airplay on the Urban and Adult R&B radio stations as well being named Billboard Magazine's number one Urban Adult Song for 2009.

p8s4.title: Uncle Charlie
p8s4.text: It debuted and peaked at number two on the Billboard 200 with sales of 58,000 copies in its first week.

p8s5.title: Uncle Charlie
p8s5.text: This was his highest peak on the Billboard 200 to date and so far has sold 362,355 copies.

p9s0.title: Hate to Feel
p9s0.text: "Hate to Feel" is the tenth track on Alice in Chains' album "Dirt" (1992).

p9s1.title: Hate to Feel
p9s1.text: The song was included on the compilation albums "Music Bank" (1999) and "The Essential Alice in Chains".

p9s2.title: Hate to Feel
p9s2.text: It has also been the ninth track on later prints of the album and eleventh on others.

p9s3.title: Hate to Feel
p9s3.text: Some editions of "Dirt" may merge this song with the then-unlisted 43-second track "Iron Gland".

question: Are the New Orleans Outfall Canals the same length as the Augusta Canal?

parsed.explanation: The Augusta Canal is approximately 13 miles long while the New Orleans Outfall Canals are 13 miles in total length.

hops.query: Are the New Orleans Outfall Canals the same length as the Augusta Canal?

p0s0.title: Augusta Canal
p0s0.text: The Augusta Canal is a historic canal located in Augusta, Georgia, United States.

p0s1.title: Augusta Canal
p0s1.text: The canal is fed by the Savannah River and passes through three levels (approximately 13 miles total) in suburban and urban Augusta before the water returns to the river at various locations.

p0s2.title: Augusta Canal
p0s2.text: It was devised to harness the water power at the fall line of the Savannah River to drive mills, to provide transportation of goods, and to provide a municipal water supply.

p0s3.title: Augusta Canal
p0s3.text: It is the only canal in the US in continuous use for its original purposes of providing power, transport and municipal water.

p1s0.title: 17th Street Canal
p1s0.text: The 17th Street Canal is the largest and most important drainage canal in the city of New Orleans.

p1s1.title: 17th Street Canal
p1s1.text: Operating with Pump Station 6, It moves water into Lake Pontchartrain.

p1s2.title: 17th Street Canal
p1s2.text: The canal, along with the Orleans Canal and the London Avenue Canal, form the New Orleans Outfall Canals.

p1s3.title: 17th Street Canal
p1s3.text: The 17th Street Canal forms a significant portion of the boundary between the city of New Orleans and Metairie, Louisiana.

p1s4.title: 17th Street Canal
p1s4.text: The canal has also been known as the Metairie Outlet Canal and the Upperline Canal.

p2s0.title: Almonaster Road
p2s0.text: Almonaster Avenue is a four-lane divided road in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States, named after 18th-century Spanish philanthropist Don Andres Almonaster y Rojas.

p2s1.title: Almonaster Road
p2s1.text: It forms in the residential neighborhoods of the Upper Ninth Ward by branching off at a Y-type intersection with Franklin Avenue.

p2s2.title: Almonaster Road
p2s2.text: Shortly afterwards, the road elevates on an overpass to cross the Norfolk Southern Railway and returns to ground level as it crosses the Industrial Canal on the Almonaster Avenue Bridge, a bascule bridge that it shares with CSX Transportation, proceeding into New Orleans East.

p2s3.title: Almonaster Road
p2s3.text: The traffic lanes straddle the railroad bridge on either side; this is the only location where Almonaster becomes a two-lane road, albeit divided.

p2s4.title: Almonaster Road
p2s4.text: It is also the last of the combination railroad/automobile movable bridges.

p2s5.title: Almonaster Road
p2s5.text: It winds through the New Orleans Business and Industrial District (NO BID) parallel with the Mississippi River Gulf Outlet and Gulf Intracoastal Waterway.

p2s6.title: Almonaster Road
p2s6.text: It intersects with Interstate 510 before finally ending at the junction with U.S. Highway 90.

p2s7.title: Almonaster Road
p2s7.text: It is also known for New Orleans street racing.

p3s0.title: Karakum Canal
p3s0.text: The Karakum Canal (Qaraqum Canal, Kara Kum Canal, Garagum Canal; Russian: Каракумский канал , "Karakumsky Kanal", Turkmen: Garagum kanaly , گَرَگوُم كَنَلیٛ, "Гарагум каналы") in Turkmenistan is one of the largest irrigation and water supply canals in the world.

p3s1.title: Karakum Canal
p3s1.text: Started in 1954, and completed in 1988, it is navigable over much of its 1375 km length, and carries 13 km3 of water annually from the Amu-Darya River across the Karakum Desert in Turkmenistan.

p3s2.title: Karakum Canal
p3s2.text: The canal opened up huge new tracts of land to agriculture, especially to cotton monoculture heavily promoted by the Soviet Union, and supplying Ashgabat with a major source of water.

p3s3.title: Karakum Canal
p3s3.text: Unfortunately, the primitive construction of the canal allows almost 50 percent of the water to escape en route, creating lakes and ponds along the canal, and a rise in groundwater leading to widespread soil salinization problems.

p3s4.title: Karakum Canal
p3s4.text: The canal is also a major factor leading to the Aral Sea environmental disaster.

p4s0.title: New Orleans Outfall Canals
p4s0.text: There are three outfall canals in New Orleans, Louisiana – the 17th Street, Orleans Avenue and London Avenue canals.

p4s1.title: New Orleans Outfall Canals
p4s1.text: These canals are a critical element of New Orleans’ flood control system, serving as drainage conduits for much of the city.

p4s2.title: New Orleans Outfall Canals
p4s2.text: There are 13 mi of levees and floodwalls that line the sides of the canals.

p4s3.title: New Orleans Outfall Canals
p4s3.text: The 17th Street Canal is the largest and most important drainage canal and is capable of conveying more water than the Orleans Avenue and London Avenue Canals combined.

p5s0.title: London Avenue Canal
p5s0.text: The London Avenue Canal is a drainage canal in New Orleans, Louisiana, used for pumping rain water into Lake Pontchartrain.

p5s1.title: London Avenue Canal
p5s1.text: The Canal runs through the 7th Ward of New Orleans from the Gentilly area to the Lakefront.

p5s2.title: London Avenue Canal
p5s2.text: It is one of the three main drainage canals responsible for draining rainwater from the main basin of the city of New Orleans.

p5s3.title: London Avenue Canal
p5s3.text: The London Avenue Canal's flood walls built atop earthen levees breached on both sides during Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

p6s0.title: Orleans Canal
p6s0.text: The Orleans Canal is a drainage canal in New Orleans, Louisiana.

p6s1.title: Orleans Canal
p6s1.text: The canal, along with the 17th Street Canal and the London Avenue Canal, form the New Orleans Outfall Canals.

p6s2.title: Orleans Canal
p6s2.text: The current version of the canal is about 2 km long, running along the up-river side of City Park, through the Lakeview and Lakeshore neighborhood, and into Lake Pontchartrain.

p6s3.title: Orleans Canal
p6s3.text: It is part of the system used to pump rain water out of the streets of the city into the Lake.

p6s4.title: Orleans Canal
p6s4.text: The Canal has also been known as the Orleans Avenue Canal, the Orleans Outfall Canal, the Orleans Tail Race, and early on, the Girod Canal,

p7s0.title: Southern Railway Terminal (New Orleans)
p7s0.text: The Southern Railway Terminal, originally officially "New Orleans Terminal", in New Orleans was constructed by the Southern Railway in 1908 on the neutral ground of Basin Street at the intersection of Canal Street.

p7s1.title: Southern Railway Terminal (New Orleans)
p7s1.text: The building was designed by Daniel Burnham, who was also the architect for the Union Station in Washington D.C.

p7s2.title: Southern Railway Terminal (New Orleans)
p7s2.text: The station also served the New Orleans and Northeastern Railroad and the New Orleans Terminal Company.

p8s0.title: 16th Ward of New Orleans
p8s0.text: The 16th Ward or Sixteenth Ward is a division of the city of New Orleans, Louisiana, one of the 17 Wards of New Orleans.

p8s2.title: 16th Ward of New Orleans
p8s2.text: It is an Uptown ward, along with the adjacent 17th Ward formerly part of the city of Carrollton, Louisiana, annexed by New Orleans in the 1870s.

p8s3.title: 16th Ward of New Orleans
p8s3.text: The Ward stretches inland from the Mississippi River, with the upper boundary being Carrollton Avenue, across which is the 17th Ward, and the lower being Lowerline Street, across which is the 14th Ward.

p8s4.title: 16th Ward of New Orleans
p8s4.text: The back boundary was the New Basin Canal, now part of the route of I-10.

p9s0.title: Canal Streetcar Line
p9s0.text: The Canal Streetcar line is a historic streetcar line in New Orleans, Louisiana.

p9s1.title: Canal Streetcar Line
p9s1.text: It is operated by the New Orleans Regional Transit Authority (RTA).

p9s3.title: Canal Streetcar Line
p9s3.text: It was redesigned and rebuilt between 2000 and 2004, and operation was reinstated in 2004 after a 40-year hiatus.

p9s4.title: Canal Streetcar Line
p9s4.text: Primarily running along its namesake street, Canal Street, it consists of two branches named for their outer terminals, totaling about 5+1/2 mi in length: "Canal - Cemeteries" (officially designated as Route 47) and "Canal - City Park/Museum" (officially designated as Route 48).

p9s5.title: Canal Streetcar Line
p9s5.text: Each branch is denoted with the red and light green colors respectively on most RTA publications.
